comparison_intro: One behavior contract, three implementations. Run the companion files and the same three acceptance tests against shared fixture data.

language_notes.sas: SAS starts at position 1 and takes a length. Explicit storage widths are 20, 3, 4 and 14. CSV loader retains quoted spaces.
language_notes.python: pandas slices start at 0 and exclude stop. Pad text to 20 before slicing; keep padding in the stored result columns.
language_notes.r: Base R substr starts at 1 and includes stop: SAS start 5, length 4 becomes R 5 through 8. sprintf pads these ASCII strings.

semantic_notes.title: Start plus length is not stop
semantic_notes.text: SAS substr(text,5,4), Python slice(4,8) and R substr(text,5,8) select the same four positions.

semantic_notes.title: Stored blanks remain data
semantic_notes.text: Input text occupies 20 positions; outputs occupy 3, 4 and 14. Short text still yields padded slices. Trim only a separate display.

tests.name: Original three-row fixture
tests.input: ABCDEFGHIJ, HelloWorld and SAS-to-Python, in original order.
tests.expected: Visible triples: ABC/EFGH/GHIJ; Hel/oWor/orld; SAS/to-P/-Python, with exact stored padding.
tests.catches: Off-by-one starts, confusing length with stop, and losing the remainder.

tests.name: Added short/full-width boundary
tests.input: Added validation inputs AB and 0123456789ABCDEFGHIJ (20 characters).
tests.catches: Slicing before padding, clipping the last character, or wrong inclusive/exclusive endpoint.

tests.name: Preservation, widths and order
tests.input: All shared rows reversed; original caller data saved.
tests.expected: Caller unchanged; returned text width 20 and outputs 3/4/14; metadata and row order retained.
tests.catches: Trimming stored results, variable output widths, caller mutation or row reordering.

scope: ASCII character inputs no longer than 20 positions; fixed valid starts 1, 5 and 7. No Unicode equivalence, invalid-position behavior or overflow claim. Edge rows are added validation only.
